anomalies.observed: Net /PIN23 contains J1.21, J1.23, J2.21, J2.23 and R10 pin 2. R10 is the 0Ω jumper that selects the Core2/CoreS3 channel-1 PWM source (its other end, R10.1, is on /PWM1). So bus pins 21 and 23 on both M5Stack bus connectors are shorted together, and pin 21's channel-1 PWM node (R10.2) is merged into the pin-23 pass-through net.
anomalies.expected: Bus pin 21 and bus pin 23 should be two independent nets. Per the specification the channel-1 PWM options are only pins 19 and 21 ("pin 19/21 for ch.1"), so pin 21 should connect only to R10 (as a PWM1_C2 node) and pin 23 should remain a standalone pass-through net like /PIN1, /PIN5, /PIN24, etc. (every other PINxx pass-through net in the netlist has exactly two nodes, J1.x and J2.x).

evidence.quote: R9–R12 (0 Ω jumpers): Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: M5Stack bus pins 21 and 23 are permanently shorted. On Core2/CoreS3 builds (R10 populated) the channel-1 PWM1 servo signal is additionally tied to bus pin 23, so an unrelated bus GPIO is driven/loaded by the servo control line (and vice-versa), which can cause signal contention or malfunction on the servo channel and on whatever function pin 23 carries; even with R10 open the two bus signals remain tied together.

parsed.summary: The netlist merges M5Stack bus pins 21 and 23 (net /PIN23), which is inconsistent with the design specification stating channel-1 PWM is available only on pins 19/21, and with every other pass-through pin being a simple two-node J1/J2 net; this short apparently ties the Core2/CoreS3 PWM1 node (via R10) to an unrelated bus pin 23.
